Your messages and contacts were restored from backup, but your identity keys couldn\'t come back across devices. Import the identity file you saved before switching phones to continue using the same identity — or start fresh with a new one.

This removes your old identity and takes you through onboarding to create a new one. Your restored messages and contacts were tied to the old identity, so they\'ll disappear from the app — and peers on the other side of any existing conversations won\'t recognize the new identity. The app will restart to finish setting up.

Your identity\'s private key is wrapped with a hardware-backed Android Keystore key. Keystore keys are tied to the app\'s install ID and don\'t cross a factory reset or device swap — even when the app data is restored from cloud backup. That\'s why messages and contacts came back but the identity couldn\'t decrypt itself.\n\nImporting the identity file you exported before switching devices lets us re-wrap the same identity with this device\'s Keystore key.

Your identity hash is a unique cryptographic fingerprint derived from your public key.

Think of it like a username that:
• Cannot be changed or duplicated
• Proves messages came from you
• Allows others to verify your identity

Your LXMF destination hash is derived from your identity and is used for sending and receiving messages.

This is what peers use to:
• Send you messages
• Find you on the network
• Add you as a contact

Your public key is the cryptographic key that enables secure messaging.

It's safe to share publicly and allows others to:
• Encrypt messages only you can read
• Verify your identity
• Establish secure communication

Seals message content with hybrid X25519 + ML-KEM-768 encryption, on top of Reticulum\'s own. Protects against an adversary who records traffic today and decrypts it once quantum computers exist.
Messages are protected only by Reticulum\'s standard encryption.
Seals whenever the recipient supports it and the link can carry the extra ~1.1 KB. Other Reticulum clients stay reachable, and slow radio links are spared the overhead.
Never sends a message that cannot be sealed. Contacts without post-quantum support become unreachable, and every message costs an extra ~1.1 KB even over LoRa.
The first message each way cannot be sealed — it carries the key that makes everything after it possible.

Forward traffic for the mesh network. When disabled, this device will only handle its own traffic and won\'t relay messages for other peers. It\'s generally not recommended for mobile devices to be transport nodes. They are less likely to maintain a fixed position in the network, and thus can negatively impact multihop routing. Enabling this will increase data usage and battery drain. However, in a BLE-only mesh, it\'s required for multi-hop messaging.

Make Zamolxis available as a shared RNS instance so other apps on this device (Sideband, rnsd, …) can route through Zamolxis\'s transport. Requires a service restart to take effect. If another app is already hosting a shared instance on this device, Zamolxis will join it as a client instead — see the Shared Instance banner.
